prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1238; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after a report that the insured's vehicle was struck while turning left at an intersection. The claimant states the other vehicle came through on the opposing approach as the turn was being completed.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy record and confirmed the driver involved is listed as a named driver on the policy in force at the time of loss.

Entry 3: Police report obtained. Responding officers confirm the claimant was present in the vehicle at the scene and the account matches the initial notice.

Entry 4: Photographs from the scene and the other driver's statement both describe the collision in the same way as the claimant. Two independent witnesses gave accounts consistent with the reported sequence.

Entry 5: Vehicle inspected. The damage is largely consistent with the impact described, concentrated on the front driver-side corner and the adjacent door panel.

Entry 6: Checked prior claim and repair history for the vehicle. No earlier damage to this area or any other area has been recorded.

Entry 7: Confirmed the loss occurred after the coverage start date. Nothing in the file points to damage existing before the policy took effect.

Entry 8: Claimant reported neck and back strain following the collision and was seen at a clinic the same day. Medical records describe symptoms that fit the type and force of this impact.

Entry 9: Checked the claimant's medical history for prior complaints involving the neck or back. No earlier injury to the same body area has been found.

Entry 10: Treatment has continued for somewhat longer than is typical for this kind of strain. Records are being requested from the treating provider to review the course of care.

Entry 11: Each conversation with the claimant has produced the same account of how the collision happened and what symptoms followed. No inconsistencies have been noted to date.
